profile.reading: This is T-Mobile Polskas Szlachecka data center complex in Warsaw, at ul. Szlachecka 49, sited away from the city center in an industrial zone away from busy streets. The complex comprises two independent buildings, Szlachecka A and the newer Szlachecka B, which completed construction in December 2021 and is described by the operator as one of its key Polish data centers, certified to the ANSI/TIA-942 and EN 50600 standards at the rated-3 level, broadly equivalent to Tier III availability. T-Mobile Poland, part of Deutsche Telekoms international operations, links the Szlachecka campus to its other Polish facilities in Krakow and Piaseczno via a dedicated data center interconnect network, allowing customers to combine colocation, cloud, and connectivity services across sites. The operator markets the Warsaw complex for enterprise hosting, dedicated servers, private and virtual cloud computing, Ethernet, VPN, and SD-WAN data transmission, and cybersecurity services. T-Mobile Polska traces its roots to Polska Telefonia Cyfrowa, founded in December 1995 and launched commercially in September 1996, which operated for years under the Era brand before rebranding as T-Mobile on June 5, 2011. Deutsche Telekom took full ownership in 2010 after a decade long shareholder dispute with French firm Vivendi, and the company is headquartered in the Sluzewiec district of Warsaw, not far from this Szlachecka data center site. T-Mobile Polska became the first Polish operator to pass 10 million subscribers by the end of 2005 and reported 13.2 million subscribers and a 30 percent market share by mid 2011, and today runs GSM, 4G LTE, and 5G mobile networks after retiring its 3G UMTS network in April 2023, alongside the enterprise data center and cloud business housed at facilities like this one.
